content.title: About
content.content: Bottled or canned coffee is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from brewed coffee extract, often sweetened and flavored with milk, sugar, or stabilizers. It is sealed in airtight containers, allowing it to stay fresh for months without losing aroma or taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ready‑to‑drink coffee in a bottle appeared in Japan in the 1970s.
In the United States, canned coffee popularity surged after Starbucks launched its Frappuccino line in the 1990s.
Bottled coffee is usually pasteurized, extending shelf life up to 12 months.
A wide range of flavors exists, from classic espresso to caramel latte and vanilla macchiato.
Aluminum cans better preserve flavor than glass because they protect the drink from light.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Boosts alertness
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, improving concentration and reducing fatigue.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption has been linked to a slight increase in metabolic rate and fat oxidation.

items.title: May lower risk of certain diseases
items.content: Regular moderate coffee intake is associated with reduced risk of Parkinson’s disease, type‑2 diabetes, and some cancers.

items.title: Improves mood
items.content: Caffeine raises dopamine and serotonin levels, which can enhance mood.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat when consuming too much coffee.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened ready‑to‑drink coffees can contain high amounts of sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or weight management.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Coffee’s natural acidity may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or acid reflux.

items.title: Additives and preservatives
items.content: Certain brands use artificial flavors, stabilizers, and preservatives that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The drink can be enjoyed cold straight from the bottle or can, or poured over ice. It can be diluted with water, mixed with milk, cream, or a sweetener. It pairs well with desserts, pastries, and breakfast items.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bottles and cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the product refrigerated, tightly sealed, and consume within 3–5 days.
